_notes: Per explicit instruction: advanced rules are always incorporated, not a togglable option. This file exists to make which specific rules that means auditable, not to make it optional at runtime.

official.description: Core rules as printed in the base GF9 rulebook. Always active regardless of advanced/standard.

advanced.description: Rules the base rulebook itself labels Advanced Game. Always active per project instruction, this is not a runtime toggle.

doubleSpiceBlow.notes: Two Spice Cards revealed per Spice Blow phase instead of one, with two separate discard piles (A and B). Each resolves independently, including its own possible Nexus.

strongholdSpiceCollection.notes: Passive income just for occupying at the time of collection, stacks if a faction occupies more than one qualifying stronghold. Independent of the normal 2/3-spice-per-force collection rate for territories with an active spice blow.

combatSpiceSupport.notes: Each force in a battle counts at full strength only if 1 spice is committed to it; uncommitted forces count at half strength. Battle Plan must declare total spice expended alongside the dialed number. Spice goes to the Spice Bank regardless of win/loss, except when a Traitor is revealed (winner owes nothing).

karamaCards.notes: In addition to the base-game effect (cancel one opponent faction advantage for the phase), advanced Karama grants each faction a unique one-time power on play. Bene Gesserit has no advanced Karama power in the base game. Full per-faction power table needs transcribing into rulesConfig or a dedicated karamaPowers.json before the bidding/battle engine can implement it, not yet done here.

expansionAdvanced.description: Advanced-game additions from the two expansions, same always-on treatment once an expansion faction is in play.

leaderSkillCards.notes: CHOAM & Richese variant, opt-in per rulebook rather than always-on, not a base advanced rule. Leaving disabled by default, revisit if wanted.

advancedStrongholdCards.notes: Same as Leader Skill Cards, an opt-in variant rather than a base advanced rule.

optional.description: True optional/variant rules (not the base game's own Advanced Game section). Off by default, distinct from the always-on advanced rules above.
optional.notes: The rulebook's Optional Rules for Alliances table (page 24) offers five named presets. Default is the original unrestricted alliance game. Worth a decision later, not urgent for Phase 1.

implementationDecisions.description: Rules that exist only because a physical-table interaction needs a digital equivalent. Every entry here must have a one-line justification so it's auditable later.

entries.justification: Physical bidding relies on players holding cards face down; digital equivalent is a sequential reveal-and-decide UI rather than simultaneous entry, to preserve bidding psychology per section 16 of the brief.

victoryVariants.notes: Confirmed directly from the base rulebook text. Solo win is 3 strongholds (or all 3 Tech Tokens if Ixian/Tleilaxu expansion is active, per that expansion's rulebook), alliance win is 4 (first player) held jointly. Two-player games use 4 regardless of alliance status.
